items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So he took me with him and we would play maybe 10 or 15 of these

ctx.x: So now the leader was happy, he was going to get me a job with the band. So now the rehearsal started. Well then they found out I couldn't read. So the leader was very nice. He said to me, "well, you play very good but you've got to learn how to read." But, he said, I have a man that maybe can help you out. So he gave me the phone number and address of a man, a piano player named Bill Fry.

Well, I met Bill Fry and Bill Fry was a piano player that played by ear. And he played all the house rent parties -- we called them chittling struts then. And they played all the house rent parties on the weekend around Chicago. So he took me with him and we would play maybe 10 or 15 of these

from Friday night over to Sunday, we'd play about 10 or 15 of them, just go from one to the other, all day long Saturday and all night Saturday night. And just play from one house rent party to the other. And the fellow would give us -- pay us a dollar and give us a plate of food like chittlings or fried chicken, or something like that. And they gambled and they danced, you know, in these apartments. And he'd let us make three passes on the crap table, you know. By that we would make ourselves five or six, maybe…
